papers.title: Cooperate or Collapse: Emergence of Sustainable Cooperation in a Society of LLM Agents
papers.how_tested: GovSim common-pool simulation (fishery/pasture/pollution) with multiple LLM agents; ablation removes the inter-round conversation phase in which agents negotiate extraction limits.
papers.finding: Without communication agents overuse the resource by ~21-22% (figure differs across arXiv versions); in dialogue agents mostly negotiate and coordinate on limits at or below the sustainable threshold, but nothing binds them.

papers.title: CoopEval: Benchmarking Cooperation-Sustaining Mechanisms and LLM Agents in Social Dilemmas
papers.how_tested: Benchmarks LLM agents in social dilemmas under four mechanism families (repetition, reputation, mediation, contracting), where contracting lets players agree on binding action-conditioned zero-sum utility transfers.
papers.finding: Contracting and mediation were the most effective mechanisms for cooperation among capable LLMs; advanced LLMs defect in one-shot dilemmas without a mechanism.

papers.title: Commitment To Cooperation With Self-Negotiated Contracts
papers.how_tested: LLM agents negotiate contracts in a spatial-temporal bargaining-plus-navigation game; contract representation varied from formal contracts that compile to executable code to natural-language contracts requiring reinterpretation.
papers.finding: Self-negotiated contracts improved cooperative outcomes beyond what was possible with ordinary trading.

papers.title: Get It Cooperating: Enhancing Generative Agent Cooperation with Commitment Devices
papers.how_tested: LLM agents given commitment devices in Prisoner's Dilemma, Public Goods, and a dynamic Harvest game.
papers.finding: Agents used commitment devices to reach the socially optimal (new) equilibrium in simple games, but gains were limited in the complex dynamic Harvest game.
papers.located_via: opened page (ML Anthology mirror https://mlanthology.org/icmlw/2024/yan2024icmlw-get/; OpenReview blocked by bot check)

papers.title: Cheap Talk, Empty Promise: Frontier LLMs easily break public promises for self-interest
papers.venue: ICLR 2026 Workshop on AI for Mechanism Design and Strategic Decision Making
papers.how_tested: Nine frontier LLMs make a public commitment announcing their intended action, then play one-shot normal-form games against each other across six games and several group sizes; deviations from the promise are classified.
papers.finding: Agents broke their public promises in ~56.6% of scenarios, mostly without saying they were doing so.

papers.title: When Agents Lie: Premeditation, Persistence, and Exploitation in Repeated Games
papers.how_tested: LLM agents play repeated n-player games under a three-stage protocol (private intent, public announcement, final action) that measures whether they keep public announcements.
papers.finding: Most deviations (>90% in the highest-deception conditions) were already planned privately; models disagreed on whether announcements were binding or cheap talk, which produced payoff gaps that persisted over all 10 rounds.

papers.title: Cheap Talk Stabilizes Strategic Interaction in LLM Agents
papers.how_tested: Pairs of open-weight 7-9B LLMs play repeated Prisoner's Dilemma, Snowdrift, Stag Hunt, and Harmony games with non-binding pre-play messages switched on or off.
papers.finding: Cheap talk mostly stabilized agents' policies; the effect varied by model and framing, with five corrected reversals in social or team framings.

papers.title: Communication Enables Cooperation in LLM Agents: A Comparison with Curriculum-Based Approaches
papers.how_tested: Multiple LLM agents play a 4-player Stag Hunt and an iterated public goods game with a one-word cheap-talk channel switched on or off, compared against an in-context curriculum.
papers.finding: The cheap-talk channel raised Stag Hunt coordination from 0% to 96.7%, while the curriculum lowered public-goods payoffs by 27.4%.

papers.title: Institutional AI: Governing LLM Collusion in Multi-Agent Cournot Markets via Public Governance Graphs
papers.authors: Marcantonio Bracale Syrnikov et al. (incl. Federico Pierucci)
papers.how_tested: Multi-LLM Cournot markets (90 runs per condition, 6 model configurations) compare no governance, a prompt-only anti-collusion rule, and a public immutable governance graph whose sanctions an Oracle/Controller runtime applies automatically, with a cryptographically keyed append-only log.
papers.finding: The institutional regime cut the mean collusion tier from 3.1 to 1.8 and severe collusion from 50% to 5.6%; the prompt-only regime gave no reliable improvement. PARTIAL for P06-04: rules execute automatically, but this is not a blockchain smart contract.

papers.title: Towards Transparent and Incentive-Compatible Collaboration in Decentralized LLM Multi-Agent Systems: A Blockchain-Driven Approach
papers.how_tested: GPT-4 agents coordinated through Solidity smart contracts for registration, task allocation, and reputation tracking, run in 50-round simulations.
papers.finding: Reports high task success, stable utility distribution, and emergent specialization. PARTIAL: the setting is task allocation, not a cooperation dilemma, and there is no condition without smart contracts.

papers.title: Do LLM Agents Negotiate Rationally? A Mechanism-Design Framework for Verifiable Multi-Agent Interaction over A2A/MCP
papers.how_tested: LLM agents bid in VCG auctions (N=30 per model) inside an A2A/MCP protocol framework, which also includes bargaining and fair-allocation tasks; the study measures truthful bidding.
papers.finding: Both models reached 100% efficient allocation, but one bid truthfully and the other did so only 3.3% of the time, so mechanism-level incentive compatibility did not carry over to LLM behaviour. PARTIAL: the abstract does not make clear whether several LLM bidders competed against each other.

papers.title: Formal Contracts Mitigate Social Dilemmas in Multi-Agent RL
papers.authors: Andreas A. Haupt et al. (with Phillip J.K. Christoffersen, Mehul Damani, Dylan Hadfield-Menell)
papers.venue: AAMAS 2023 as 'Get It in Writing: Formal Contracts Mitigate Social Dilemmas in Multi-Agent RL' (https://www.ifaamas.org/Proceedings/aamas2023/pdfs/p448.pdf)
papers.how_tested: Markov games are extended so RL agents can voluntarily agree to binding, condition-contingent reward transfers before acting (MOCA training), tested on static games and on traffic, pollution, and common-pool-resource domains.
papers.finding: Given a rich enough contract space, all subgame-perfect equilibria become socially optimal, and contracting improved welfare empirically.

papers.title: Learning to Negotiate via Voluntary Commitment
papers.how_tested: Markov Commitment Games in which RL agents may voluntarily commit to proposed future plans, with a commitment protocol learned by policy gradient plus incentive-compatible learning.
papers.finding: Converged faster and reached higher returns than baseline methods in mixed-motive tasks.

papers.title: Emergent Communication through Negotiation
papers.how_tested: RL agents negotiate with an ungrounded cheap-talk channel alongside a grounded proposal channel; self-interested and prosocial agents are compared.
papers.finding: Self-interested agents did not use the cheap-talk channel effectively, while prosocial agents learned to use it.

papers.title: Truthful and Trustworthy IoT AI Agents via Immediate-Penalty Enforcement under Approximate VCG Mechanisms
papers.venue: IEEE Internet of Things Journal (2026, per arXiv)
papers.how_tested: Multi-agent RL bidders trade energy in an approximate-VCG double auction with a one-shot penalty for misreporting; allocation accuracy and penalty level are varied.
papers.finding: Learned agents converged to truthful reporting near the theoretically predicted penalty threshold, and better allocation accuracy reduced incentives to deviate.

papers.title: Principal-Agent Reinforcement Learning: Orchestrating AI Agents with Contracts
papers.how_tested: A learning principal designs outcome-contingent payment contracts for learning agents under hidden action (moral hazard), tested on random binary game trees and a multi-agent Coin Game.
papers.finding: The meta-algorithm converges to subgame-perfect equilibrium contracts. PARTIAL: these are moral-hazard incentive contracts, not risk- or history-based premiums.

mechanism_updates.llm_evidence: Cheap talk switched on/off: piatti2024cooperate (GovSim no-communication ablation), madmoun2025communication, lore2026cheap. Promise stage measured: shi2026cheap, shi2026agents.
mechanism_updates.marl_evidence: cao2018emergent: self-interested RL agents ignore cheap talk; prosocial agents use it.
mechanism_updates.seed_claims_checked: GovSim communication result: confirmed (21-22% overuse without communication, depending on arXiv version).

mechanism_updates.llm_evidence: Binding action-conditioned transfers/contracts: tewolde2026coopeval (contracting among the most effective mechanisms), wyse2026commitment (self-negotiated contracts), yan2024get (commitment devices in PD/PGG/Harvest).
mechanism_updates.marl_evidence: haupt2022formal (binding reward-transfer contracts, MOCA); zhu2025learning (Markov Commitment Games).
mechanism_updates.seed_claims_checked: GovSim 'agents state intentions, soft commitment': mischaracterized. GovSim has only non-binding conversation and implements no commitment (that belongs under P06-01). The seed's 'partial' status is superseded by the direct tests above.

mechanism_updates.llm_evidence: No LLM study found with escrowed upfront deposits or bonds. Contract transfers (tewolde2026coopeval, haupt2022formal) are ex-post transfers, not deposits. yan2024get's commitment devices may include deposit-like mechanisms; not verifiable from the abstract.
mechanism_updates.seed_claims_checked: 'Not yet tested': confirmed within the search bounds.

mechanism_updates.llm_evidence: Code-enforced auto-execution without a blockchain: wyse2026commitment (contracts compiled to code), bracale2026institutional (governance graph applied automatically by an Oracle/Controller). Actual Solidity smart contracts but not a dilemma: qi2025towards.
mechanism_updates.seed_claims_checked: 'Discussed (Pierucci et al. 2026)': partly confirmed. The Pierucci-first-author framework paper (arXiv 2601.10599) is conceptual and its abstract does not mention smart contracts. The empirical companion (Bracale Syrnikov, Pierucci et al., 2601.11369) tests auto-enforced rules, not smart contracts. Status raised from discussed to partial.

mechanism_updates.llm_evidence: No LLM study found with enforced no-take zones or taboo periods.
mechanism_updates.marl_evidence: None found. Commons Harvest-style MARL has no enforced no-take rule.
mechanism_updates.seed_claims_checked: 'Partially tested via GovSim hard extraction ceiling': mischaracterized. GovSim enforces no per-agent or group ceiling: the sustainability threshold is information only, and the resource collapses if stock falls below C=5.

mechanism_updates.llm_evidence: Keeping public announcements measured: shi2026cheap (promises broken in ~56.6% of scenarios), shi2026agents (announcement vs final action). Partial: piatti2024cooperate (agents agree limits in public dialogue; not isolated as a manipulation).
mechanism_updates.marl_evidence: zhu2025learning: voluntary commitment to future plans, but not public/reputational in the human sense.
mechanism_updates.seed_claims_checked: GovSim pre-round communication as public commitment: confirmed as partial (agents coordinate on limits in dialogue; no commitment condition is manipulated separately).

mechanism_updates.llm_evidence: No LLM multi-agent cooperation study found that imposes hard rate or extraction limits as a manipulated mechanism.
mechanism_updates.seed_claims_checked: 'Partially tested via GovSim extraction ceiling': mischaracterized. GovSim has no enforced ceiling (see P06-05).

mechanism_updates.llm_evidence: albayaydh2026llm: LLM agents in VCG auctions; truthful bidding depends on the model (one truthful, one 3.3%). Unclear whether LLM bidders interact. Other LLM-auction work (Auction Arena 2310.05746; Shah et al. 2507.09083) uses ascending/first/second-price formats, not VCG, and 2507.09083 compares LLMs with human benchmarks rather than LLM vs LLM; both excluded.
mechanism_updates.marl_evidence: shao2025truthful: MARL bidders converge to truthful reporting under approximate VCG plus penalty.
mechanism_updates.seed_claims_checked: 'Not yet tested in LLM social dilemma context': still true for social dilemmas specifically. An auction-setting study now exists (partial).
'Not yet tested': confirmed within the search bounds.

mechanism_updates.llm_evidence: None found (LLM voting simulations use approval or ranked-choice rules, not quadratic funding).
mechanism_updates.seed_claims_checked: 'Not yet tested': confirmed within the search bounds.

mechanism_updates.llm_evidence: No premium mechanism found. Malenfant 2026 'Moral Hazard in Multi-Agent Language Models' (arXiv 2607.23982) studies a moral-hazard game with varied query costs but no history-based premium; excluded.

notes: (1) Excluded but relevant for other slices or the verifier: Pierucci et al. 2026 'Institutional AI: A Governance Framework for Distributional AGI Safety' (arXiv 2601.10599; conceptual, counts as 'discussed'); Sun et al. 2023 'Cooperative AI via Decentralized Commitment Devices' (arXiv 2311.07815; NeurIPS 2023 MASEC workshop position paper, no learning-agent experiments; 'discussed' for P06-02/P06-04); AI Economist (Zheng et al., Science Advances 2022, doi 10.1126/sciadv.abk2607; MARL tax design is general mechanism design, not VCG/TCR/QF/premium, so it may belong under a taxation/incentive primitive); d'Eon et al. EC'24 (arXiv 2402.19420; MARL bidders in iterative combinatorial clock auctions, not VCG); Chen et al. Auction Arena (arXiv 2310.05746; LLMs in ascending auctions, not a truthful mechanism); Shah et al. (arXiv 2507.09083; LLM bidders vs human benchmarks, not LLM vs LLM); Bracale Syrnikov et al. 'Draining the Energy Commons' (arXiv 2607.22188; 12-LLM commons with no quota or rate-limit intervention, useful as a P06-07 baseline). (2) GovSim figures differ across arXiv versions (21% vs 22% overuse without communication; 62% vs 54% negotiation share); cite the version used. (3) CoopEval venue 'ICML 2026' and the Shao et al. IEEE IoT J. venue come from arXiv metadata; confirm against the proceedings. (4) Haupt et al.: arXiv title is 'Formal Contracts Mitigate Social Dilemmas in Multi-Agent RL', first author Haupt on arXiv; the AAMAS 2023 version is titled 'Get It in Writing: ...' and the author order there should be checked (often cited as Christoffersen et al.). (5) yan2024get is a workshop paper on OpenReview with no arXiv ID; the full text was not opened, so which commitment devices it uses (possibly deposits, which would affect P06-03) is unverified. (6) Recent 2026 arXiv items (lore2026cheap, wyse2026commitment, albayaydh2026llm, shi2026agents) are preprints; albayaydh2026llm's multi-LLM interaction in the VCG task is unconfirmed (HTML 404). (7) Gaps: deposits/bonds (P06-03), no-take zones (P06-05), hard rate limits (P06-07), TCR (P16-02), and quadratic funding (P16-03) have no artificial-agent tests in either track; smart contracts have only non-dilemma or non-blockchain analogues.
